title: graceful prefetch window smoothing and admission hysteresis for continuous-batcher
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Continuous batching has periodic p99 spikes and occasional KV-cache starvation when many short requests interleave with a few long ones. This PR adds a smoothing layer for prefetch window sizes, an admission hysteresis gate to reduce oscillation under bursty load, and a lightweight KV-weighted aging heuristic to prevent pin-starvation. The change is intentionally conservative: we add configurable knobs with safe defaults to avoid accidental throughput regressions.

Design summary: (1) Prefetch window smoothing keeps a moving exponential average of the effective prefetch size per slot and limits instantaneous growth by a configurable growth_clamp factor. (2) Admission hysteresis introduces two thresholds: admit_threshold and release_threshold (release_threshold < admit_threshold) so we only shrink prefetch windows after sustained low-utilization, avoiding thrash. (3) KV-weighted aging biases slot reclamation away from slots with large KV pin counts by assigning an "effective age" that scales inversely with pinned_kv_count, preventing eviction storms for KV-heavy requests. (4) Timeout micro-tuning: we shift from a uniform hard timeout to a jittered soft-timeout that lets a small fraction of near-deadline requests run to completion before preemption, which reduces tail amplification for conversational workloads.

Implementation notes: Changes are primarily in runtime/batcher/continuous_scheduler.{cc,h}, runtime/kv/kv_pin_tracker.{cc,h} and runtime/config/defaults.go. New feature flags: batcher.prefetch.smoothing.enabled, batcher.admission.hysteresis.{admit,release}, batcher.kv_age.weight. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve existing behavior unless smoothing or hysteresis flags are toggled; config validation rejects obviously unsafe values.

Benchmarks and testing: Microbench harness (perf/bench/continuous_bench) shows a 7% reduction in p99 latency and a 3% increase in median throughput on our mixed short+long synthetic workload (50k requests, 90/10 short/long split). KV-heavy regression suite (perf/kv_starvation_suite) shows elimination of recurring slot reclamation for pinned workloads in 95% of runs. Unit tests and integration tests added for hysteresis transitions, smoothing window boundary conditions, and KV aging math.

Rollout plan: Merge to main, enable feature flags off by default. Canary rollout to dedicated/intra-team redwood clusters for 48 hours with telemetry gates: p99 latency, batching efficiency, slot churn rate, and KV eviction events. If telemetry remains stable, flip smoothing.enabled=true and hysteresis to conservative values across hosted rows over 7 days.

Risks and mitigations: Overly-aggressive smoothing could reduce responsiveness to persistent load shifts — mitigated by growth_clamp and per-tenant overrides. Admission hysteresis can delay capacity reductions; thresholds chosen to be conservative and runtime metrics expose hysteresis dwell time. KV-weighted aging is intentionally gentle to avoid starving short stateless requests; can be disabled per-deployment.

Related: ENG-4107 (batcher tuning epic), ENG-4210 (kv pinning observability), SUP-1201 incident postmortem referenced in the description.

This description is intentionally compact but covers motivation, design, tests, and rollout instructions.
